entries.claim: On held-out test transitions the size of the frame-to-frame contact change is associated with the hand's speed relative to the contacted object: Spearman 0.785 [0.767, 0.801] on TACO (22,932 transitions) and 0.513 [0.413, 0.621] on ARCTIC (11,718). This same-step association, stronger on TACO than on ARCTIC, is what motivated asking whether the hand also predicts the change ahead of time.
entries.metric: Spearman rank correlation between d_t = ||C_{t+1} - C_t|| (one-step contact change) and the speed of the hand relative to the contacted object, over test transitions; interval = take-cluster bootstrap (200 replicates in build_hand_cache.py). Higher = stronger same-frame association; it is not a prediction score.
caveats: This is a same-transition association (hand speed and contact change at the same step), not predictive information.
The TACO value uses the tool-frame transform corrected in this study; the earlier temporal-event report gives 0.68 for the same quantity.
It is a sanity statistic of the cache build, not one of the study's designed comparisons.
ARCTIC's interval is wide (44 takes in the test set).
entries.claim_as_extracted: On held-out test transitions the size of the frame-to-frame contact change is strongly associated with the hand's speed relative to the object (Spearman 0.78 on TACO, 0.51 on ARCTIC); this association is why the study asks whether the hand also predicts the change ahead of time.
entries.correction_reason: Values confirmed. 'Strongly' fits TACO; ARCTIC's 0.51 with an interval down to 0.41 does not carry the same adjective. Use 0.785 for TACO: the report and INDEX print 0.79, the extractor 0.78, and the cell is 0.7848. It is a sanity statistic of the cache build (200 take-bootstrap replicates), same-step, not a prediction score. The motivating earlier report printed 0.68 for TACO (wrong tool-frame transform).

entries.claim: Adding the current ground-truth hand pose to a predictor that already sees the current contact map, the object geometry and the object motion does not lower the error of the predicted 4-frame contact change on either dataset (TACO +2.3 % on the 3-seed mean, the same size as an uninformative shuffled-hand input; ARCTIC -0.3 %, interval includes 0).
entries.metric: Paired per-frame difference of E_Delta(4) = L2 norm of (predicted - true C_{t+4} - C_t), raw contact units, seed mean of 3 seeds, condition F1 (F0 + current hand pose) minus F0 (no hand), over all valid test frames; rel_to_F0_pct = 100 * diff / mean error of F0. Lower (negative) = better. Interval = take-level cluster bootstrap 95 % (1000 replicates). Test set: TACO 364 sequences / 186 takes, ARCTIC 186 / 44.

caveats: TACO's 'worse' is seed-dependent: in seed 2 the pose model is slightly below the no-hand model; the interval is a take bootstrap of the 3-seed mean and carries no seed variance. Safe wording: no gain; worse on the 3-seed mean on TACO.
The pose is not useless for the other task on TACO: it gives the small transition-start AUPRC gain (+0.027, see the transition entry).
Hands are ground truth; one architecture (100 hand surface points, flattened, through a small encoder) under a recipe fixed on the no-hand model.
The no-hand predictor F0 already sees object motion up to 8 frames ahead (the object trajectory is a given input of the task).

entries.claim: A causal hand history (ground-truth hand positions at the current and the 8 previous frames) gives a small gain in predicting the 4-frame contact change (-2.4 % of the no-hand error on TACO, -2.1 % on ARCTIC; paired intervals exclude 0), and the 8 frame-to-frame hand displacements without absolute pose give more (-6.8 % / -4.2 %). Against a shuffled-hand control of the same input size the gains hold on TACO (-4.6 % history, -9.0 % motion-only) and are not distinguishable from zero on ARCTIC's all-frame mean L2 error (-0.1 %, -2.2 %; intervals include 0). At the 8-frame horizon TACO's gains stay (-2.9 % / -6.3 %) and ARCTIC's intervals include 0 (-1.1 % / -2.2 %).
entries.metric: Paired per-frame difference of E_Delta(h) (L2 error of the predicted contact change, raw contact units, seed mean of 3 seeds) between two conditions over all valid test frames, with take-cluster bootstrap 95 % interval (1000 replicates); rel_to_F0_pct = difference in % of the no-hand model's mean error on the same frames. Lower (negative) = better. F2k8 = F0 + hand positions of frames t-8..t (the report's primary causal condition); F2rel = F0 + the 8 one-frame hand differences (motion only); F2shuf = F2k8 with the hand history of another sequence (capacity control).

entries.claim_as_extracted: A causal history of the last 8 ground-truth hand frames gives a small gain in predicting the 4-frame contact change (-2.4 % of the no-hand error on TACO, -2.1 % on ARCTIC), and frame-to-frame hand motion without absolute pose gives more (-6.8 % / -4.2 %); against a shuffled-hand control of the same size the gain holds on TACO (-4.6 % / -9.0 %) and is not distinguishable from zero on ARCTIC's all-frame mean error.
entries.correction_reason: Numbers confirmed. The history condition reads frames t-8..t, i.e. 9 frames, not 'the last 8'. The h = 8 dataset difference belongs in the claim, not only in a caveat. Per-seed means agree with the direction (history and motion-only below no hand in all 3 seeds on both datasets), but the intervals are take bootstraps of the seed mean and carry no seed variance.

entries.claim: A non-causal oracle that is also given the next 8 ground-truth hand frames lowers the same error much more (-17.7 % of the no-hand error on TACO, -15.6 % on ARCTIC; 10.8 % / 11.4 % of the no-hand error beyond the best causal input, intervals exclude 0). Adding only one future frame gives -0.7 % (TACO) / -2.4 % (ARCTIC) against the no-hand model on all frames at the 4-frame horizon (derived value, no interval), which is no more than the causal inputs give. This is consistent with most of the hand-contact coupling lying inside the predicted multi-frame window, with a smaller part visible in the past hand.

entries.claim_as_extracted: A non-causal oracle that is also given the next 8 ground-truth hand frames lowers the same error far more (-17.7 % on TACO, -15.6 % on ARCTIC), while one future frame adds almost nothing at the 4-frame horizon (-0.7 % / -2.4 %); this is consistent with hand and contact changing together over the predicted window rather than the past hand announcing the change.
entries.correction_reason: Numbers confirmed. 'Rather than the past hand announcing the change' erases the small causal gains that the same tables show (intervals exclude 0). 'Adds almost nothing' is an all-frames statement: on TACO the +1 oracle gives -7.5 / -9.0 / -25.7 % on persistent spatial / mixed / release frames (report Table 5, confirmed in history_length_ablation.csv), and on all frames it is significantly worse than the causal motion-only model on both datasets (Ffut1-F2rel +6.1 % / +1.9 %).

entries.claim: Per frame, the causal gain is largest on release frames on both datasets (motion-only: -20.4 % of the no-hand error on TACO, -15.4 % on ARCTIC), followed by onset and amount-dominant frames (motion-only -10.6 % / -11.1 % on TACO, -10.3 % / -8.0 % on ARCTIC); persistent mixed frames gain -7.0 % (TACO) / -5.6 % (ARCTIC). Persistent spatial frames gain -4.2 % (history) / -5.6 % (motion-only) on TACO and nothing on ARCTIC (+1.6 % / +3.0 %, intervals include 0), where the +8-frame oracle's -8.3 % also has an interval that includes 0. Transient frames gain least: TACO -0.4 % (interval includes 0) / -1.8 %; ARCTIC no gain, and motion-only is significantly worse there (+9.4 %, n = 76).

Frame class = the dominant (largest) spike event among the transitions inside the 4-frame window: quiet (non_spike) when none is a spike; otherwise transient (a low-persistence change), onset, release (incl. onset+release), amount, persistent spatial, persistent mixed.

entries.claim_as_extracted: Per frame, the causal gain is largest on release, onset and persistent mixed contact changes (motion-only on release: -20.4 % on TACO, -15.4 % on ARCTIC) and smallest where contact re-arranges at roughly constant amount: persistent spatial frames gain -4.2 % / -5.6 % on TACO and nothing on ARCTIC, where even the +8-frame oracle's -8.3 % has an interval that includes 0.
entries.correction_reason: Every quoted cell is confirmed, but the ranking is not what the table shows. (1) The amount-dominant class (TACO n = 176, ARCTIC n = 89) was left out; its causal gain is second only to release on both datasets. (2) On TACO the motion-only gain on persistent mixed frames (-7.0 %) is smaller than on quiet frames (-7.7 %) and close to persistent spatial (-5.6 %), so 'mixed' is not among the largest there. (3) The smallest gain is on transient frames on both datasets, not on persistent spatial frames. 'Roughly constant amount' is a paraphrase of the rule 'amount share of the change <= 0.3'.

dataset_differences: Only TACO and ARCTIC were run; OakInk2 has no result in this study (no cached hand state in the object frame).
Same-step association of contact change with hand speed: Spearman 0.785 on TACO, 0.513 on ARCTIC.
Current pose (h = 4, all frames): TACO +2.3 % (worse on the 3-seed mean, interval excludes 0, but seed-dependent); ARCTIC -0.3 % (interval includes 0).

Shuffled-hand control vs no hand (h = 4): TACO +2.2 % (worse), so TACO's causal gains exceed the control (history -4.6 %, motion -9.0 % of the no-hand error); ARCTIC -2.0 % (interval includes 0), so on ARCTIC's all-frame mean L2 neither the history (-0.1 %) nor motion-only (-2.2 %) is distinguishable from the control. On ARCTIC only the per-class gains (release, onset, persistent mixed) exceed the control; in squared error the ARCTIC history does beat the control at h = 4.
Size of the causal gain: motion-only -6.8 % on TACO vs -4.2 % on ARCTIC at h = 4; at h = 8 TACO stays significant (-2.9 % history, -6.3 % motion) while ARCTIC's intervals include 0 (-1.1 %, -2.2 %).

Persistent spatial frames (h = 4): TACO gains -4.2 % (history) / -5.6 % (motion), oracle +8 -24.9 %, all intervals exclude 0; ARCTIC +1.6 % / +3.0 % (no gain), oracle +8 -8.3 % with an interval that includes 0.
Transient frames (h = 4): TACO -0.4 % (n.s.) / -1.8 % (small, significant); ARCTIC +5.6 % (n.s.) / +9.4 % (motion-only significantly worse; n = 76).
Quiet (non-spike) frames (h = 4): TACO motion-only -7.7 % (significant, n = 15846); ARCTIC -2.5 % (interval includes 0).
Release frames (h = 4): history -10.9 % (TACO) vs -6.6 % (ARCTIC); motion-only -20.4 % vs -15.4 %; oracle +8 -44.8 % vs -47.8 %.

Baseline standing (h = 4): the no-hand predictor is 8.2 % better than predicting no change on TACO and 11.9 % worse on ARCTIC (mean L2); on ARCTIC even the oracle +8 is not significantly better than no change.

Transition-start AUPRC (h = 4): TACO 0.332 without the hand (chance 0.098), causal inputs +0.03 (paired intervals exclude 0, gain comes from the current pose); ARCTIC 0.133 (chance 0.062), no causal input differs significantly and the absolute history is lower (0.120). The oracle's gain is larger on ARCTIC (+0.151) than on TACO (+0.095) and on ARCTIC sits in the release / regrasp positives (one-vs-rest AUPRC 0.042 -> 0.257).
Motion-only vs absolute history on the transition task (h = 4): ARCTIC +0.022 AUPRC (interval excludes 0); TACO -0.001 (no difference).
Recall at precision 0.5: at h = 8 TACO's no-hand classifier already reaches 0.50 (history 0.57, oracle 0.68); ARCTIC stays at or below 0.04 for causal models (oracle 0.21).
One future frame at the one-step horizon (h = 1): on TACO the oracle +1 (0.274) is clearly below the causal motion-only model (0.299); on ARCTIC it is not (0.178 vs 0.174).
Sample and stability: TACO test set 364 sequences / 186 takes, ARCTIC 186 / 44, so ARCTIC intervals are much wider; ARCTIC causal models reach their best validation loss after about 300 steps.
do_not_claim: Hand motion is irrelevant to (or independent of) contact change: the same-step association is strong (Spearman 0.78 TACO / 0.51 ARCTIC) and the future-hand oracle shows the information exists.
The hand causes, or does not cause, contact change: 'causal' here means only that the input uses hand frames at or before the current frame; nothing was intervened on.

Causal hand history carries no information / gives no gain: the gains are small but several have intervals that exclude 0 (TACO beyond the shuffled control; release, onset and persistent mixed frames on both datasets).

The past hand cannot predict transition timing at all, or transition timing is unpredictable: on TACO the causal inputs add a small significant AUPRC gain (+0.03) and the no-hand model is already far above chance (0.332 vs 0.098).
'10-28 % on release' as a result for both datasets or against one baseline: it is a TACO range mixing 'vs no hand' and 'vs shuffled control'; ARCTIC is 6.6-17.6 %.
'Causal history gives 2-7 %' as an ARCTIC statement without the control: ARCTIC's range is 2.1-4.2 % and its absolute-history gain equals the shuffled control in mean L2.
A single pooled number such as 'the oracle helps by about 17 %': report TACO (-17.7 %) and ARCTIC (-15.6 %) separately.
The oracle shows what a hand-contact co-evolution model would achieve: it uses ground-truth future hands and is an upper bound on information; generated hands were never tested.
Hand and contact are simultaneous, stated as an established mechanism: the tables are consistent with a largely simultaneous coupling (the report's 'Case D' reading).
Persistent spatial contact changes are unexplained by the hand in general: on TACO the +8 oracle removes 24.9 % and the causal inputs 4-6 %; the null is ARCTIC's.
On ARCTIC the +8 oracle beats predicting no change: its improvement interval includes 0; and every causal ARCTIC predictor is worse than predicting no change in mean L2.
The current hand pose makes prediction worse, as a robust effect: it is the 3-seed mean on TACO, reversed in one seed, and absent on ARCTIC; and the pose is what helps the TACO transition classifier.

Dynamics matter, static configuration does not, as a general law: it was measured with one architecture and one hand representation (100 surface points, flattened), with exceptions listed in the caveats.
The hypotheses or decision cases were pre-registered: no plan file exists for this study; say 'the hypotheses and decision cases stated in the report'.
The oracle +1 bar has a confidence interval or a paired test against the no-hand model: no such row exists; the value is the sum of two paired rows.
Overlapping per-condition error bars in the AUPRC figure mean 'no difference' (or non-overlap means a significant difference): the paired differences are the test.
The gain is confined to release / onset / mixed frames: on TACO the motion-only input also lowers the error on quiet frames (-7.7 %).

The Figure F example panels are representative: per dataset they are the two events where the 8-frame history helped most and the two where it hurt most, from seed-0 models; they are dense research panels with internal labels and are not page-ready.
Any OakInk2 statement for this block.
The 'No-Go for co-evolution' is an experimental result: it is the report's design decision drawn from these numbers.
